the regulation of brain and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) calcium (Ca) following vitamin D‐related chronic hypo‐ or hypocalcemia.

the regulation of brain calcium (Ca2+) by brain barrier membranes in chronic hypo‐ and hypercalcemia.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vitamin D deficiency or toxicity has no effect on brain Ca homeostasis, which is maintained by a mechanism that does not seem to be mediated by vitamin D3 metabolites.
the central nervous system is protected from changes in plasma calcium by a saturable transport system at the brain barrier membranes.
the brain and CSF are protected from changes in extracellular calcium levels by a homeostatic mechanism that is not dependent upon 1,25(OH)2 vitamin D3.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is protected from the effects of hyper‐ or hypocalcemia.
the brain and CSF are not as tightly regulated as plasma [Ca] during chronic hypocalcemia.
the brain has a remarkable capacity to maintain normal calcium homeostasis in the face of severe changes in plasma calcium.
